 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of death of one Mohammed Matin, who is the son of the petitioners No.1 & 2 and brother of Petitioners No.3 & 4 in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in brief is as follows:
MVC No.1442 of 2022 That on 10.03.2022 at about 8.15 p.m., when the deceased Mohammed Martin was riding his motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-01-EZ-3391 along with his friend Kumari Rohini from Maramma Circle towards Yeshwanthpura, C.V.Raman Road, near Jimkhana Gate, at that time, a Towing Vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-01-AB- 6553, which was being driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came from back side of the motorcycle of the deceased and dashed to the motor cycle of the deceased, as a result of which, the said Mohammed Martin and his friend Rohini Sahani both fell down and Mohammed Martin sustained multiple grievous injuries on his body.
Immediately he was taken to Ramaiah Hospital, where he was reported to be dead.
A case was registered against the driver of the Towing Vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-01-AB- 6553 in Crime No.30/2022 of Yeshwanthpura Traffic Police Station.
Hence, this petition for compensation.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, respondent No.1 appeared through its Counsel and filed written statement.
The respondent No.2 though appeared through his counsel, but not chosen to file written statement.
4. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the entire petition averments as false.

It has admitted that insurance MVC No.1442 of 2022 policy was issued by it in respect of Commercial vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AB-6553 in favour of the 2nd respondent which was valid from 02.08.2021 to 01.08.2022.

The alleged accident, if any, was due to the own negligence of the deceased himself, he was unmindful of the traffic and movement of the vehicles on road, without following lane discipline and traffic rules, without giving way for other vehicles, without any signal or indication and without wearing helmet, went to the middle of the road and came across the insured towing vehicle.
There was no accident caused by the insured towing vehicle, as there is no visible damage caused to the insured towing vehicle, as per the report of the Motor Vehicles Inspector.

The jurisdictional police without proper investigation, deliberately and dishonestly registered an accident case against the driver of the insured Towing vehicle, which is a bigger vehicle, only to help the petitioners.
The petitioners are not entitled to any compensation from the respondents.
The amount of compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
The petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties and hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Court has framed the following issues:
MVC No.1442 of 2022 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that on 10.03.2022 at about 08.15 p.m., on C.V.Raman Road, near Gymkhana Gate in Yeshwanthpura of Bengaluru City, the deceased Mohammed Matin being rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-01-EZ-3391 had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Towing Vehicle bearing No.KA-01/AB-6553 by its driver and the deceased succumbed to injuries sustained in the accident as averred ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that this petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation and If so, what amount and from whom?
4. What order and award ?
6.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioner No.1 got himself examined as PW-1 and got marked documents at Exs.P.1 to P.21.

The respondents have got examined two witnesses as RWs 1 and 2.
7.
Heard the arguments on both sides.

My findings on the above issues are as under :
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...

As per final order, for the following:-
REASONS MVC No.1442 of 2022 9. Issue No.1 : The petitioners in order to prove this issue, are relying upon th evidence of PW.1 and documentary evidence such as FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV Report, Inquest Mahazar, PM Report, notice under Sec.133 of M.V. Act, reply to the said notice, police intimation and chargesheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.

PW.1 being the father of the deceased in his affidavit evidence, has narrated the manner in which his son met with an accident and accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553.
Though the second respondent being the owner of the towing vehicle appeared through his counsel, but he has not contested the petition by filing the written statement.
Only the first respondent who is the insurer of the said towing vehicle has filed written statement by denying the accident and also negligence aspect.

10. It is the contention of the first respondent that the deceased himself without following the lane discipline and traffic rules and without giving any signal or indication and without wearing helmet,
went to the middle of the road and came across the insured towing vehicle and due to his negligence,
deceased met with an accident and no accident was caused by the insured towing vehicle, as there is no visible damages caused to the said vehicle, but the jurisdictional MVC No.1442 of 2022 police without proper investigation have registered a false case against the driver of the insured towing vehicle, which is a big vehicle only to help the petitioners to have wrongful gain.
In order to prove its contention, the first respondent has placed the evidence of driver of the towing vehicle as RW.1 and its official as RW.2.
Let us consider the evidence placed by the parties to decide this issue.

11. As per PW.1, when his son was riding motorcycle along with pillion rider on 10.03.2022 at about 8.15 p.m., from Maramma Circle towards Yeshwanthapura on C.V.Raman road, Bengaluru, at that time a towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553 came in a rash and negligent manner from the backside of the motorcycle and dashed to the motorcycle and as such, both the rider and the pillion rider fell down on the road and then his son was shifted to Ramaiah hospital, wherein his son was declared as dead.
Admittedly, PW.1 has not seen the accident.
PW.1 admits that complaint was lodged by one Rohini Sahani.
Even the complaint-Ex.P.2 discloses that the said Rohini Sahani was a pillion rider on the motorcycle of the deceased on the date of accident and she has sustained injuries in accident.
The petitioners have not examined the said Rohini Sahani who is said to be an eye-witness.
As such, we have to decide this issue on the basis MVC No.1442 of 2022 of the evidence of RW.1 and on the basis of the documents produced by the petitioners.

12. Exs.P.1 & P.2 disclose that on the basis of the complaint lodged by Rohini Sahani, a criminal case was registered against the driver of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553 on the date of accident.

Ex.P.3 is the crime detail form and Ex.P.4 is the spot sketch which reveals the Mohammed Munir vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180554192/
4 state of affairs at the accident spot.

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.3, the place of accident is on C.V.Raman road near IISC Zimkhana ground and there is a center median in the middle of the road and by the edge of the road there is foot path.

In Ex.P.3 it is mentioned that the accident spot is shown in alphabet 'A', the place where blood stains found is shown at alphabet 'B', the movement of the motorcycle is shown at alphabet 'C', the movement of towing vehicle is shown at alphabet 'D' and the electric pole is shown at alphabet 'E' in the sketch.
Ex.P.4 is the said sketch consisting of the said details.
Ex.P.4 discloses that C.V.Raman road is a two way road having center median.
In Ex.P.4, the movements of both the vehicles are shown one after the other.
That means, as per Ex.P.4, motorcycle of the deceased was moving in front of towing vehicle and manner of accident is shown as motorcycle hit by towing vehicle.

PW.1 in his cross-examination has admitted that the road on which the accident MVC No.1442 of 2022 took place is a two way road and there is a divider in between the road and as per the skecth-Ex.P.4, accident took place in the middle of the road and there is no signal light or zebra cross near the accident spot and Bengaluru-Tumkur road is a busy road having thick population of movement of people and vehicles.

These admissions of PW.1 supports the state of affairs mentioned in Ex.P.4.
13.

As per RW.1 who was the driver of the towing vehicle as on the date of accident, on 10.03.2022 when he was driving the said towing vehicle on the left side of the road from Sadashivanagar towards Yeshwanthapura, on his right side a car was moving and on his left side a bike was moving and the said bike rider in order to overtake another two wheeler came behind his vehicle from left side and touched the middle portion of his vehicle, due to which, the rider and pillion rider of the bike fell down on the left side.
That means, as per RW.1, the deceased himself touched the towing vehicle and due to it, the deceased fell down on the left side.
The above evidence of RW.1 is contrary to the state of affairs shown in Ex.P.4.

RW.1 has denied that the motorcycle was moving ahead of his vehicle and he was behind the said motorcycle and as per Ex.p.4, motorcycle was moving in front of his vehicle and he dashed his vehicle to the motorcycle and due to his fault, accident took place.
As per RW.1, he MVC No.1442 of 2022 has not given complaint to the police by stating that accident had not occurred due to his fault.

The evidence of RW.1 is contrary to the contention taken by the first respondent wherein it is stated that the rider of the motorcycle came across the insured towing vehicle without giving way for other vehicles and without any signal or indication.
RW.1 is the person who was at the spot at the time of accident.
Such being the case, the contention of the first respondent that the deceased came across the insured towing vehicle and due to his own negligence accident occurred cannot be believed.

14. RW.2 who is an official of the first respondent company, in his affidavit evidence has deposed that the chargesheeted driver has deposed before the court that the deceased rider in the process of overtaking a vehicle moving in front, went to the right side of the road at high speed in rash and negligent manner and by loosing control over the motorcycle, he fell down on his own in front of the towing vehicle.

But, RW.1 has deposed that when the deceased was moving on a bike on the left side of his vehicle, in order to overtake another vehicle, came behind his vehicle from left side and touched in the middle of towing vehicle and as such, the rider fell down on the left side.
Hence, the evidence of RW.2 with respect to the manner in MVC No.1442 of 2022 which accident took place is contrary to the versions of RW.1 in his evidence.

sentences.text: The evidence of RWs 1 and 2 is contrary to the police documents produced before the court.
In the sketch-Ex.P.4, the movement of the motorcycle of the deceased is shown in front of the towing vehicle and the place of accident is shown on the left side of the road.

That means, both the vehicles were moving one after the other and the motorcycle of the deceased was moving in front of the towing vehicle and not on the back side of towing vehicle as contended by the first respondent.
It is noticed that the chargesheet has been filed against RW.1, but he has not challenged it.
Even he has not given any counter complaint to the police by stating that accident had not occurred due to his fault.

Such being the case, only on the evidence of RWs 1 and 2, it is not possible to believe that accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of RW.1.
16.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report which discloses that there were no fresh visible damages found on the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553.
In Ex.P.5, it is mentioned that rubbing marks found on right hand side of the mask and right hand side rear MVC No.1442 of 2022 view mirror of the motorcycle of the deceased were damaged.
The first respondent in its written statement has contended that as the IMV report discloses that no damages are found on the towing vehicle, accident was not caused by the said vehicle.
Even RW.2 has deposed the said fact.

Merely because no damages are found on the towing vehicle, the claim of the petitioners cannot be doubted since normally if a big vehicle hits a small vehicle, damages will not be found on the big vehicle.
Therefore, only on the said fact, it is not possible to believe that no accident was caused by the towing vehicle.
17. Ex.P.6 is the Inquest report and Ex.P.7 is the PM report which discloses that the death of the deceased was due to multiple injuries sustained in accident.
Ex.P.8 is the police notice issued to the second respondent by the police under Sec.133 of the M.V Act and Ex.P.9 is the reply given by him.
In Ex.P.9, the second respondent has stated that accused in criminal case was the driver of towing vehicle as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.10 is the police intimation issued by Ramaiah Medical College Hospital to Sadashivanagar police regarding the death of the deceased.
Ex.P.11 is the chargesheet filed by the police against the driver of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553.
This chargesheet has not been challenged by RW.1.
RW.1 in his cross-examination has admitted that criminal case MVC No.1442 of 2022 registered against him is still pending.

If at all there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the towing vehicle i.e.,
RW.1, then he would have definitely challenged the chargesheet filed against him.
But, RW.1 has not done so.
This conduct of RW.1 enables the court to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he remained silent.
Even the evidence of RW.2 is of no help to the first respondent to prove its contention, since he has given evidence on the basis of police documents, but he has no personal knowledge about it.
Therefore, the evidence of RWs 1 and 2 is of no help to the first respondent to prove its contention regarding accident and negligence aspect.

On the other hand, the petitioners by producing the documentary evidence, have satisfactorily proved that the deceased met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553 by its driver and thereby he succumbed to the injuries.

18. The learned Counsel for the petitioners during his argument has relied upon the decision reported in 2014 ACJ 2648 (Ashwinbhai Jayantilal Modi Vs. Ramkaran Ramchandra Sharma &

sentences.text: In the present case also, there is no direct evidence showing negligence of the deceased that led to the accident as discussed above.

Such being the case, contributory negligence cannot be attributed to the deceased when the evidence on record satisfactorily proves that accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2 :

The first respondent in its written statement has contended that as the petitioners have not impleaded the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-01-EZ-3391 as parties to the petition, the petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties.
As discussed in Issue No.1, absolutely there is no evidence before the court to believe that the accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Whereas, there is evidence which proves that the deceased met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the towing vehicle by its driver.
Such being the case, I am of the opinion that the owner and the insurer of the motorcycle are not necessary parties.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 in the Negative.
Issue No.3 : Petitioners claim that they are the parents and brothers of the deceased Mohammed Matin.

In order to prove their relationship, they have produced their Aadhaar cards and also the Aadhaar card of the deceased, DL of the deceased and Death Certificate of the deceased as per Exs.P.14 to P.20.
These documents disclose that the deceased was the son of Petitioners No.1 & 2 and brother of petitioners No.3 & 4.

As such, it can be said that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased and they are entitled to claim compensation on account of the death of the deceased.
21.
PW.1 has deposed that his son was aged about 21 years earlier to accident.

In order to prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners are relying upon Aadhaar card and DL of the deceased as per Exs.P.18 and P.19 wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 09.11.2000.
Even the same date of birth is shown in his ID card at Ex.P.12.
By considering the said date of birth, it can be said that the deceased was aged about 21 years as on the date of accident.

22. PW.1 has deposed that prior to the accident, deceased was studying 3rd year BDS at Rajiv Gandhi College of Dental Sciences and Hospital, Bengaluru and due to the death of his son, they have MVC No.1442 of 2022 suffered irreparable loss and damages.

PW.1 has deposed that the deceased was an outstanding student of medicine and the deceased would have pursued his M.D.
after graduation and would have reached greater heights, since there is tremendous increase in demand for medical professionals and there is rise in the salaries of the doctors.
PW.1 has produced college ID card as per Ex.P.12, which discloses that the petitioner was a student of BDS in Rajiv Gandhi College of Dental Sciences and Hospital.

sentences.text: PW.1 has produced the fee receipts at Ex.P.13 which discloses that PW.1 has met the educational expenses of the deceased.
As the deceased was a student of BDA prior to accident, he was not an earning person.
As such, notional income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration by considering his future earnings as a doctor.
In this regard, I intend to rely on a decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Rajbala & Anr.

sentences.text: (M/s United India Insurance Co.Ltd.) (MAC.APP.462/2018) DD 22.10.2018.

In the said case, considering the fact that the deceased was a final year student of B.Tech at Maharshi Dayananda University, Rohtak, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has taken the earning capacity of the deceased as Rs.25,000/- per month.
In the case on hand, at the time of accident, the deceased was a third year student of BDS.
PW.1 has produced MVC No.1442 of 2022 the marks card of the deceased at Ex.P.21, which is pertaining to the first year BDS.
The deceased has passed first year BDS in first attempt.
As per PW.1, his son had a good future and he would have taken care of them in their old age.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.30,000/- per month, as the accident was of the year 2022.

23. As per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others), 40% of the income of the deceased has to be taken as future prospects.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 40% of the present income of Rs.30,000/- is Rs.12,000/-.

If the same is added to deceased personal income, it comes to Rs.42,000/-.
24.
As per PW1, as the deceased was a bachelor, he was residing with the petitioners.
Hence, it can be safely held that the petitioners are the dependents on the income of the deceased.
As per Sarla Verma's Case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, 50% of the income of the deceased requires to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, if he had been alive.
After deducting the same from Rs.42,000/-, the balance comes to Rs.21,000/-.
The annual income of the deceased works out MVC No.1442 of 2022 to Rs.2,52,000/-.
As I have already discussed above, as on the date of accident, deceased was aged 21 years.
As per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation) the multiplier applicable to the present case is 18.

entities.text: 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If we multiply the annual income of the deceased by 18 multiplier, the same works out to Rs.45,36,000/-.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled to Rs.45,36,000/- towards loss of notional income and this amount would be awarded to the petitioners under the head Loss of Dependency.

25. As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 2017 ACJ 2700 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Praney Sethi and others) under the conventional heads, the petitioners are awarded Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses.

As per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in (2018)18 SCC 130 (Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd.,
Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others), loss of filial consortium has to be awarded to the petitioners No.1 & 2.

In view of the above said reasons, I am inclined to award compensation to the petitioners under the following heads:

Thus, the petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.46,57,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of the petition till realisation.

So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioners, the first respondent is the insurer and the second respondent is the owner of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553.

The first respondent in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553 in favour of the second respondent and also the validity of the policy from 02.08.2021 to 01.08.2022.
Accident occurred on 10.03.2022.
As such, the policy was valid as on the date of accident.

As discussed in Issue No.1, this court has come to the conclusion that the petitioners have proved that the deceased met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553 by its driver resulting in the death of the deceased.

So the respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.46,57,000/- to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
28. Issue No.4 :

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3, and for the reasons stated therein, I proceed to pass the following: -

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioners is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 & 2, awarding compensation of Rs.46,57,000/- (Rupees Forty Six Lakhs Fifty Seven thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.1, being the Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
The compensation amount is apportioned amongst the petitioners No.1 to 4 at the ratio of 40:30:10:20.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% share of the petitioners No.1 to 3 with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their respective names in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.

Remaining 50%
with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioners No.1 to 3.
The share of petitioner No.4 who is a minor, shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of the choice of Petitioner No.1, till he attains the age of majority.

MVC No.1442 of 2022 Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of death of one Mohammed Matin, who is the son of the petitioners No.1 & 2 and brother of Petitioners No.3 & 4 in a road traffic accident.
A case was registered against the driver of the Towing Vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-01-AB- 6553 in Crime No.30/2022 of Yeshwanthpura Traffic Police Station.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
Mohammed Munir vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180554192/
2 3.
The alleged accident, if any, was due to the own negligence of the deceased himself, he was unmindful of the traffic and movement of the vehicles on road, without following lane discipline and traffic rules, without giving way for other vehicles, without any signal or indication and without wearing helmet, went to the middle of the road and came across the insured towing vehicle.
There was no accident caused by the insured towing vehicle, as there is no visible damage caused to the insured towing vehicle, as per the report of the Motor Vehicles Inspector.
The jurisdictional police without proper investigation, deliberately and dishonestly registered an accident case against the driver of the insured Towing vehicle, which is a bigger vehicle, only to help the petitioners.
The petitioners are not entitled to any compensation from the respondents.
The amount of compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
The petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties and hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Court has framed the following issues:
MVC No.1442 of 2022 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that on 10.03.2022 at about 08.15 p.m., on C.V.Raman Road, near Gymkhana Gate in Yeshwanthpura of Bengaluru City, the deceased Mohammed Matin being rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-01-EZ-3391 had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Towing Vehicle bearing No.KA-01/AB-6553 by its driver and the deceased succumbed to injuries sustained in the accident as averred ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that this petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation and If so, what amount and from whom?
4. What order and award ?
6.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. It is the contention of the first respondent that the deceased himself without following the lane discipline and traffic rules and without giving any signal or indication and without wearing helmet,
went to the middle of the road and came across the insured towing vehicle and due to his negligence,
deceased met with an accident and no accident was caused by the insured towing vehicle, as there is no visible damages caused to the said vehicle, but the jurisdictional MVC No.1442 of 2022 police without proper investigation have registered a false case against the driver of the insured towing vehicle, which is a big vehicle only to help the petitioners to have wrongful gain.
Hence, the evidence of RW.2 with respect to the manner in MVC No.1442 of 2022 which accident took place is contrary to the versions of RW.1 in his evidence.
Mohammed Munir vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180554192/
5 15.
Such being the case, only on the evidence of RWs 1 and 2, it is not possible to believe that accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of RW.1.
16.
Merely because no damages are found on the towing vehicle, the claim of the petitioners cannot be doubted since normally if a big vehicle hits a small vehicle, damages will not be found on the big vehicle.
Therefore, only on the said fact, it is not possible to believe that no accident was caused by the towing vehicle.
Even the evidence of RW.2 is of no help to the first respondent to prove its contention, since he has given evidence on the basis of police documents, but he has no personal knowledge about it.
On the other hand, the petitioners by producing the documentary evidence, have satisfactorily proved that the deceased met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553 by its driver and thereby he succumbed to the injuries.
In the present case also, there is no direct evidence showing negligence of the deceased that led to the accident as discussed above.
Such being the case, contributory negligence cannot be attributed to the deceased when the evidence on record satisfactorily proves that accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the towing vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-6553.
As such, notional income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration by considering his future earnings as a doctor.
Mohammed Munir vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180554192/
7 Vs. Sumit Dahia & Ors.
(M/s United India Insurance Co.Ltd.) (MAC.APP.462/2018) DD 22.10.2018.
If the same is added to deceased personal income, it comes to Rs.42,000/-.
24.
As per PW1, as the deceased was a bachelor, he was residing with the petitioners.
Hence, it can be safely held that the petitioners are the dependents on the income of the deceased.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled to Rs.45,36,000/- towards loss of notional income and this amount would be awarded to the petitioners under the head Loss of Dependency.
As per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in (2018)18 SCC 130 (Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd.,
Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others), loss of filial consortium has to be awarded to the petitioners No.1 & 2.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioners No.1 & 2 being the parents of the deceased are entitled for loss of filial consortium at Rs.44,000/- each and as such the petitioners No.1 & 2 are awarded Rs.88,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.
In view of the above said reasons, I am inclined to award compensation to the petitioners under the following heads:

i Monthly Income 30,000-00 Mohammed Munir vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 16 January, 2024
iv Compensation 2,52,000x18 45,36,000-00  after multiplier  applied  v Loss of estate 16,500-00
Thus, the petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.46,57,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of the petition till realisation.
So the respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.46,57,000/- to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.

9 MVC No.1442 of 2022 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 & 2, awarding compensation of Rs.46,57,000/- (Rupees Forty Six Lakhs Fifty Seven thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.1, being the Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
The compensation amount is apportioned amongst the petitioners No.1 to 4 at the ratio of 40:30:10:20.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% share of the petitioners No.1 to 3 with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their respective names in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50%
with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioners No.1 to 3.
The share of petitioner No.4 who is a minor, shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of the choice of Petitioner No.1, till he attains the age of majority.
